WITH RECURSIVE
-- Base case: direct callers of term_len
base AS (
  SELECT caller_symbol_id AS symbol_id, 1 AS hops
  FROM code.calls
  WHERE callee_symbol_id = 'src/click/_compat.py::term_len'
),
-- Recursive case: callers of the base callers (hops = 2)
recursive_cte AS (
  SELECT c.caller_symbol_id AS symbol_id, b.hops + 1 AS hops
  FROM code.calls c
  JOIN base b ON c.callee_symbol_id = b.symbol_id
  WHERE b.hops = 1
)
-- Combine both levels, remove duplicates keeping the minimum hops
SELECT symbol_id, MIN(hops) AS hops
FROM (
  SELECT symbol_id, hops FROM base
  UNION ALL
  SELECT symbol_id, hops FROM recursive_cte
)
GROUP BY symbol_id
ORDER BY symbol_id, hops;

request:
Which functions or methods in the click library (src/click/) reach term_len (src/click/_compat.py) within at most two direct calls: either calling it directly, or directly calling a repository function or method that itself calls term_len directly? Count only calls written as a plain function name or as a method call on self; calls through other objects (e.g. formatter.write_dl(...)) and passing a function as an argument do not count. Give the symbol ID and the minimum number of calls in the chain (1 for a direct caller, 2 otherwise).

Requested output columns: symbol_id (string), hops (integer).
explanation: The query uses a recursive CTE to first identify all direct callers of term_len (hops=1), then finds all callers of those callers (hops=2). It combines both levels and selects the minimum hops for each symbol, ensuring each function/method appears only once with its shortest call chain length.
